title: batchMint lacks nonReentrant; ERC1155 onERC1155Received callback fires mid-loop
description: BatchNFTMinter does not inherit ReentrancyGuard (unlike sibling NFTStaker). ERC1155 _mint invokes onERC1155Received on the caller-chosen recipient mid-loop (per iteration, before forceApprove(0) at line 242 and the nudge payout at line 246) while max approval is live, paymentAmount is held, and the nudge pot is intact.
impact: Defensive gap only. Adjudicated NOT-EXPLOITABLE for third-party fund loss on current code: full-balance payout is idempotent to zero, held paymentAmount is the attacker's own per-call budget, max approval is bounded to the contract's own balance, and NFTStaker has independent OZ-guarded storage. Becomes HIGH only if the payout is changed to fixed-amount or a per-caller balance is retained.
attackPath: 1. Reentrancy is reachable (recipient callback mid-loop) but no state read after the callback can be manipulated to extract extra funds on current code.
Defensive gap only; becomes High only under speculative future changes (fixed-amount payout or retained per-caller balance).
recommendation: Add OZ nonReentrant to batchMint for parity with the sibling NFTStaker and defense-in-depth against future payout changes.
